newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ofwat says leaks lower but still work to do.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ofwat says leaks lower but still work to do.

text.p: Britain's water and sewerage companies have managed to cut leaks by around nine percent in 1996-97, but there is still work to do, industry regulator Ofwat said on Wednesday.
"I expect to see a substantial reduction in leakage in the run up to the 1999 price review," Ofwat head Ian Byatt said in a statement.
Byatt said he welcomed progress made by some companies, including North West Water, now part of United Utilities, and Severn Trent, which had made "particular headway on previous years".
But he added that "others are still showing little improvement".
Ofwat said it would now discuss the figures with the Environment Department, the Welsh Office and the Environment Agency.

The new Labour government has been fiercely critical of water companies and called a crisis summit to improve the industry in May at which it said mandatory targets for cutting leaks would be set by Ofwat.
Ofwat will issue a full report on water deliveries, including details of next year's mandatory targets for cutting leaks, in the autumn.
Ofwat also said that consumption figures could have "an important influence on reported leakage", adding that it considered the range on consumption to be "excessive".
